title: Made sergeant, playing bass, and the president's rebuke
summary: Made a top sergeant, Thomas filled in on bass for a parade and was then listed to play it. He skipped the parade, was called before President Nathan B. Young, was busted, and still had to write a notebook for graduation.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: School days: grades, teachers and leaving school

blocks.x: a thing happened that I didn't care for at all. So out of the blue, they made me a top sergeant. I didn't ask for it and think I didn't realy make it was necessary. So, our trumpet player didn't show. I mean our bass player didn't show. We had this big, elegant bass, you know. Big, elegant bass that winds up in the air.

Yeah, you know. No, this was a silver one. I don't know where they got this. So they get ready to march but the player bass player didn't show so I told them that I'd play the bass. It's a B flat instrument and we'd march up and down the hills. You know, it's a hilly town. Jeff City is a hilly town. You walk up and down and it's hotter than the hinges of hell. So we made it through. Most of the marches I knew they were going to play. So we made it through. So we came back and everybody salute is applauding us and they've got this little bit going, you know, which I didn't care for. So, the next time we got ready to march -- incidentally, my duties were to form the company. Form the company A, B and whatever the company's names were and report to the lieutenant, "Your company is formed, sir." Which, you know, what the hell, they got it. So, on the bulletin board --
now this guy had just come from Tuskegee.

No, the commandant and we didn't care too much for him. He meddled in our affairs. He got too -- I'd been there two years now, you know, I'm damn near president. Two years, from Webster Groves, too. "You ain't kidding." So, on the bulletin board, he puts up that -- I don't know why I looked at the bulletin board because I never do, never did in those days. I happened to look at it that day. It says the following non-commissioned officer, Joseph L. Thomas, in the course of our parade today will play bass. I didn't know I sounded that good.
This was after your first performance?
Yeah, I didn't know I sounded that good. So I said to myself I'll play nothing. So I didn't show. I didn't make the parade at all which they were unhappy about.
Well, you didn't want to play the bass anyway.

I didn't want to march. I didn't want to play the trumpet really. I had enough of that marching business so I didn't show. So then I was called into the president's office and Nathan B. Young was the president then at that time. And, I got the real treatment. So I told him, "Well, Mr. President, this is my instrument. The trumpet is my instrument

and I don't care for the ROTC in the first place. And I don't care to march and I know nothing at all about the bass." He said, "Mr. Thomas, you'll have to cooperate." I said, "I am the best of cooperating, Mr. President, to/my knowledge." He said, "What did you do?" I said, "I stayed at home. Stayed in my dormitory." He said, "That won't do at all." And I said, "Well, why, Mr. President?" He said, "Because we're bringing in ROTC here for a trial period and we want it to go." I said, "Is it my curriculum?" He said, "No, it isn't." I said, "Then why should I do it?" It must be left to my choice. Do I want it or don't want it. So, anyhow, during the course of Lincoln -- Lincoln was tremendous. It only had 300 students. Very close and warm. And this incident ... they had an idea. Say, well, the following non-commissioned officer, Joseph L. Thomas, is busted. I said, "Well, who cares." But, now comes graduation time. My mother and father are coming to school to see me graduate. Those cats made me write up a two year notebook. What do I care about reconnoitering, you know? And all that sort of thing but I had to do it. I mean I didn't have to do it but my parents were coming there so we did it.
